summary: Intermittent duplicate external tool/webhook calls due to idempotency-token drift on client reconnect (clock skew)
description: Customer reports duplicate external webhook invocations (payment capture endpoint) after transient network disconnects during streaming/function-calling sessions. Duplicates occur sporadically — often after mobile carrier transitions or VPN re-keys. Customer payloads show same conversation context but different idempotency token values generated on reconnect, resulting in double side-effects (double charge).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming function-call session with the Redwood TS SDK pointed at a private deployment behind PayFast.ai's VPC proxy. 2) During a long-running conversation that triggers a 'capture_payment' tool, forcibly drop the client network (VPN toggle / airplane mode) for ~5-20s. 3) Reconnect the client and allow the SDK to automatically resume streaming. 4) Observe that the SDK replays the function call but generates a fresh idempotency token (timestamp-based nonce) on reconnect; the server treats it as a new invocation and forwards to customer's webhook.
logs:
[2026-03-10T14:22:08.123Z] request_id=01F3A0 client=session=xx-3 reconnect=true idempotency=token=1628134328 nonce=1628134328 tool=capture_payment webhook_forward=sent
[2026-03-10T14:22:08.347Z] request_id=01F3A1 client=session=xx-3 reconnect=true idempotency=token=1628134334 nonce=1628134334 tool=capture_payment webhook_forward=sent
Customer webhook received two POSTs within 1s: trace_ids 01F3A0 / 01F3A1; payloads identical except idempotency header values.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: SDK uses epoch-second or time-based nonce for per-action idempotency token; when client clock or monotonic base shifts during disconnect/reconnect, SDK emits a different token and server cannot collapse duplicates. Verified with customer that their mobile client had ~7s clock drift during VPN re-key. Reproduced in lab by manipulating client clock and toggling streaming reconnect with TS SDK v1.4.2. Python SDK v0.9.8 and Go SDK v0.14 show similar behavior if configured to use 'timestamp' mode for idempotency keys. Server-side dedupe only performs exact token match or a short session-hash window currently; does not compute canonical tool-call fingerprint unless token absent. Potential contributing factors: multiplexing/replay logic in SDK sends resumed chunks with regenerated per-action metadata, and proxy (customer side) injects small additional latency changing timestamp granularity.
comments: Support (Mariana): Customer provided webhook logs showing duplicate charge IDs. Asked Eng for urgent triage due to financial risk.

SRE (Evan): Captured request traces from prod gateway. Confirmed two distinct request_ids and two forwarded webhook POSTs. Noted idempotency header mismatch: X-Redwood-Idempotency differs. Investigating SDK behavior on resume.

Eng (Daniel Kim): Reproduced locally by simulating clock jump + reconnect in TS SDK. Found code path where SDK regenerates action token using Date.now() on resume; previous action token not preserved in session state. Opened PR to persist per-action nonce across reconnects.
Customer (PayFast.ai, Olivia Chen): Provided SDK logs and mobile OS network debug. Agrees to test SDK patch in staging. Asks for mitigation to avoid more duplicate charges in prod meanwhile.

Support (Mariana): Provided temporary mitigation: enable server-side blocking rule to deduplicate by (session_id, tool_name, payload_hash) within 60s window and throttle webhook forwarding for this customer. Raised billing hold with Finance to reverse duplicates.
resolution_notes: Short-term: Applied server-side customer-scoped dedupe rule for PayFast.ai (session_id+tool+sha256(payload) within 60s) and enabled webhook delivery backoff to 10s for second attempts to reduce immediate double charges. Finance issued manual refunds for the two affected transactions. Long-term: SDK patches merged: SDK-TS PR #462 persists per-action idempotency tokens in session state and switches default token generation to UUIDv4 + monotonic counter (no reliance on system clock). SDK-Python and SDK-Go patches (PRs linked) will follow. Serving runtime update: added optional tool-call fingerprinting fallback that will dedupe by (tool_name, payload_hash, session_id) for 120s when tokens differ. Docs updated with "Idempotency and reconnect" guidance; recommended customers upgrade SDKs and avoid client-side clock adjustments during active sessions. Follow-up: release notes and client rollout scheduled for 2026-03-20; monitor metrics and set alert for webhook duplicate rate >0.1%.
follow_up_actions: Backport SDK fixes to 1.x maintenance branches and publish security advisory
Add automated test coverage for reconnect + clock drift scenarios in SDK e2e tests
Create runbook entry: support guide for stuck/replayed tool calls due to clock skew
Monitor PayFast.ai's webhook duplicate metric for 7 days
public_notes: If you rely on time-based idempotency tokens in client SDKs, consider switching to UUIDv4 + monotonic counters that are resilient to client clock changes. We recommend upgrading Redwood SDKs to versions that implement this pattern. For private deployments, request enabling server-side session fingerprint deduping as a stopgap.
customer_impact: Customer reported 2 confirmed double-charge incidents affecting 3 end-users; potential for broader impact if other mobile clients on the same carrier experience VPN re-key events. High business impact due to payments.
